variants.name: protobuf FieldMask + FieldMaskUtil::TrimMessage
variants.implementation_notes: Where the wire format is an IDL-generated protobuf message, the projection is data: the receiver (or its caller) sends a FieldMask naming the retained paths and FieldMaskUtil::TrimMessage(mask, &msg) removes every field not listed, projecting the message in place before it is serialized. What replaces the classic filter object is the mask plus one library call, and because the mask is data it can differ per request or per receiver without new code. Trimming drops required fields of fields not named in the mask unless TrimOptions::set_keep_required_fields(true) is used, so for proto2 messages decide that explicitly; outside protobuf (plain JSON/custom wire formats) the classic hand-written projection struct is still the fallback.
pitfalls: TrimMessage mutates the message in place: anything else holding that message (a cache, an audit log, another consumer) now sees the trimmed version.
Required fields are trimmed by default when they are not named in the mask - pass TrimOptions with keep_required_fields(true) if the receiver validates the schema.
A mask path that no longer exists in the .proto is a runtime error only when the mask is checked; keeping masks as unknown paths degrades silently in hand-written implementations.

variants.name: narrow projection struct (no IDL)
variants.idiom_name: hand-written view struct + projection function (std::optional for absent fields)
variants.implementation_notes: Without an IDL or a serialization library, the projection is a type: define a view struct that holds only the retained fields and a function that copies them out of the domain object, using std::optional (or a sentinel) where a field is conditionally omitted; std::string_view keeps the copy cheap as long as the source outlives the view. What replaces the classic filter object is the type boundary itself - a field that has no member in the view cannot be serialized by accident. Hand-written recursive filtering over a parsed document remains justified when the retained field set is supplied as data (a runtime mask) rather than fixed at compile time, but then the mask needs the same contract test the struct would have got for free.
pitfalls: A view made of string_view/optional references is only valid while the source object lives - returning one from a function that owns the source yields a dangling projection.
std::optional distinguishes 'absent' from 'empty'; mapping a missing field to std::nullopt and an empty string to "" must be a deliberate contract, or receivers cannot tell them apart.
Without a schema check the struct and the producer's message can drift apart silently: nothing in the compiler notices that the producer renamed a field, only the contract test does.
